extraction.name: LongBench
extraction.description: LongBench is the first bilingual, multi-task benchmark for long context understanding, enabling a more rigorous evaluation of long context understanding. LongBench comprises 21 datasets across 6 task categories in both English and Chinese, with an average length of 6,711 words (English) and 13,386 characters (Chinese). These tasks cover key long-text application areas including single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion.
extraction.creator: Yushi Bai, Xin Lv, Jiajie Zhang, Hongchang Lyu, Jiankai Tang, Zhidian Huang, Zhengxiao Du, Xiao Liu, Aohan Zeng, Lei Hou, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, Juanzi Li
extraction.publisher: Tsinghua University, Zhipu.AI, Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
extraction.citeAs: Yushi Bai et al. (2023). LongBench: A Bilingual, Multitask Benchmark for Long Context Understanding. arXiv:2308.14508v2 [cs.CL]
extraction.rai:dataCollection: LongBench is composed of 21 datasets across 6 major task categories. 6 datasets are directly extracted from original datasets provided by previous studies, 10 are built based on original datasets and processed to be suitable for long context evaluation, and 5 are created and annotated by the authors. Data collection includes extraction from public datasets (NarrativeQA, Qasper, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, DuReader, GovReport, QMSum, MultiNews, VCSUM, TREC, TriviaQA, SAMSum, LSHT, LCC, RepoBench-P) and manual curation (MultiFieldQA-en, MultiFieldQA-zh, PassageCount, PassageRetrieval-en, PassageRetrieval-zh).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sources include: Literature and Film (NarrativeQA), Science papers (Qasper), Wikipedia (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, TriviaQA, PassageCount, PassageRetrieval-en), Baidu Search and Baidu Zhidao (DuReader), Government reports (GovReport), Meeting transcripts (QMSum, VCSUM), News articles (MultiNews, LSHT), Web questions (TREC), Dialogues (SAMSum), GitHub code repositories (LCC, RepoBench-P), C4 Dataset (PassageRetrieval-zh), and multiple sources for MultiFieldQA including legal documents, government reports, encyclopedias, academic papers from Arxiv, C4 Dataset, WuDaoCorpora, Chinese Judgements Online, Wikipedia, and Chinese Government Website.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For multi-document QA tasks, complete Wikipedia passages encompassing supporting or distracting paragraphs were used as context. Supporting passages were included within the context, and then as many distracting passages were added until the total length reached a maximum length. Finally, these passages were randomly ordered to form the multi-document context. For DuReader, for each question, several documents related to the question were provided along with arbitrarily selected documents as distractors, until each question was associated with 20 documents. For few-shot learning tasks, for each test data, an integer within a range was randomly selected as the number of examples, then the corresponding number of samples were randomly sampled from the training set and concatenated to form the context. For PassageRetrieval tasks, 30 passages were randomly sampled and one was selected for summarization using GPT-3.5-Turbo. For PassageCount, several passages were randomly selected from English Wikipedia, each paragraph was repeated at random several times, and finally the paragraphs were shuffled.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: All 21 datasets in LongBench are standardized into a unified format. Two extraction strategies were employed: random sampling to maintain natural length distribution (LongBench) and uniform sampling based on data length to study model capabilities across varying context lengths (LongBench-E). For LongBench-E, 13 English datasets were selected with uniform sampling across length ranges of 0-4k, 4k-8k, and 8k+ words. Data were extracted from test sets of public datasets to avoid test leakage, with the exception of VCSUM due to insufficient data in its test set. When input length exceeded the maximum context length of a model, the input sequence was truncated from the middle.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For MultiFieldQA-en and MultiFieldQA-zh, three Ph.D. students were invited to annotate questions and answers for each article, with definitive answers as much as possible for ease of automated evaluation. During annotation, it was ensured that answers could be inferred from the documents, and the placement of evidence was fairly random to avoid biases. Annotation guidelines specified: Questions should be as clear as possible and have definitive and relatively short answers; distribution of evidence paragraphs should be as random as possible throughout the article; questions should have varied types including information-extracting questions, summarizing questions, and multi-hop reasoning questions. The average time taken to annotate each data sample in MultiFieldQA was around 5 minutes. Cross-validation among annotators showed a 100% accuracy rate of the annotated answers.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: The annotators involved in MultiFieldQA annotation are Ph.D. students with extensive research experience in the field of NLP, positioning them as expert annotators.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-3.5-Turbo was used to generate summaries for the PassageRetrieval tasks.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors note that the placement of evidence was made fairly random during annotation to avoid biases that might occur if answer-related statements were frequently found at the beginning or the end. For multi-document QA tasks, distracting passages were randomly ordered to form the multi-document context to avoid positional biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper identifies several limitations: (1) Potentially unreliable automatic metrics (ROUGE-L, F1) may not accurately reflect response quality, particularly underestimating models that generate longer responses. (2) Performance on LongBench is coupled with models' instruction-following capabilities, as mastering the tasks demands a certain level of instruction-following capability. (3) The benchmark may not fully disentangle long context ability from task ability. (4) Some models may rely on memorization rather than context understanding, particularly for datasets derived from Wikipedia which is a common source for training LLMs.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: LongBench is designed for evaluating large language models' long context understanding capabilities across multiple tasks and languages. The benchmark enables assessment of models on: single-document QA, multi-document QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion. It is intended for Testing and Validation of LLMs with long context capabilities. The paper notes that LongBench and LongBench-E serve as ideal testbeds for future research in long context modeling.
